# Gb walks into a agriculture, food & harvest firm

Walk into any agriculture, food & harvest outfit and watch for ten minutes. You will see a very old act performed with newer props. The act has a name. It is **Gb**.

## Before the Office, the Story

**Parted from Nut.** Born of Shu and Tefnut, Geb and Nut loved without space between them until Shu, on Ra’s command, wrenched them apart — and the world’s breathable distance dates from that separation.  Geb’s green fertility and Nut’s starry vault remain arched apart for eternity, the air god’s arms the only thing between them.

**The Five Children on the Epagomenal Days.** Though the birth of the five gods belongs to Nut’s myth, the Pyramid Texts address Geb as their father and as the mountain of the west on which the dead king ascends.  ‘You are Geb, the heir of the gods,’ the utterances tell the king — the earth is the ultimate estate of succession.

## The Reveal, Seat by Seat

### Agriculture, Food & Harvest

*The earth-god whose body is the soil — grain, gold, and cattle all rise from Geb.* The match is not poetic license. Strip the trade to its function and the function is the myth.

### Mining & Natural Resources

Now read the why-line with the office in mind: *The earth is his body and his treasury — gold, ore, and grain are mined from the god himself.* The people doing this work did not borrow the archetype. They re-derived it — the way Gb was always going to be re-derived wherever earth, vegetation, snakes matters.

### Home, Hearth & Real Estate

*The ground itself as god — real estate's most literal patron: the earth one stands on.* Nobody in that trade worships at this temple. They just keep its hours.

## Not the First Rebrand

The Greeks identified Geb with their own earth — Cronos in the common equation, which made mythographic sense of his fatherhood of the divine generation.  Through Plutarch this mapping circulated widely, though Egyptian theology itself kept him younger and more fertile than the aged Titan. The office is only the latest translation.
